title: Conversion sprint template — Dedicated → Private + SLA paths
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working sprint template for Customer Success to convert mid-market Dedicated customers into either a Dedicated upsell (more capacity / SLA) or a Private deployment with premium SLA. Primary use: 6–10 week conversion sprint run by a CSM + Solutions Engineer. Goal: produce an actionable account plan, tech validation checklist, commercial proposal, and QBR-ready slide pack.

When to use this template:
- Customer shows steady growth in token spend (>= 30% QoQ) or repeated capacity throttling events.
- Security/compliance ask escalates (SOC2, KMS, VPC peering, on-prem evaluation).
- Renewal window within 90–180 days and CS health score >= 6 but with feature gaps.

Quick summary of outcomes:
1) Recommended path (Dedicated upgrade | Private deployment + managed onboarding | Add premium SLA add-on)
2) Estimated ARR uplift and TTM (time to ramp)
3) Technical feasibility note (pass/fail with open blockers)
4) Executive sponsor alignment and approvals checklist

Sprint overview (6–10 weeks)
- Week 0: Intake + health review (CSM) — gather usage trends, latency/cost anomalies, contract term, risk signals.
- Week 1: Internal kickoff — align with Solutions Eng, Sales AE, and legal on constraints. Prepare SAQ/ROI model.
- Week 2: Customer technical workshop — deployment architecture options, network/egress, KMS, data residency.
- Week 3: Commercial sketch — draft pricing with uplift buckets (capacity tiers, SLA tiers, migration credits).
- Week 4: Exec alignment — present internal recommendation and obtain approval to present to customer.
- Week 5: Customer exec QBR + proposal delivery — present benefits, migration path, ROI.
- Week 6–10: Negotiation + migration pilot planning + contract signoff.

QBR slide outline (customer-facing)
- Title slide: Customer name, date, CSM + SE contacts.
- Current state: usage, latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens, SLO breaches (if any).
- Pain drivers: specific incidents (timestamps), feature gaps, security asks.
- Option A — Dedicated capacity upgrade: benefits, expected latency improvements, cost delta, timeline.
- Option B — Private deployment: network diagram, security/compliance map, expected unit cost, onboarding ETA.
- Option C — Premium SLA add-on: service windows, escalation path, price.
- ROI model: projected token throughput, per-token cost change, 12/24 month ARR impact.
- Migration checklist & proposed timeline.
- Ask & next steps: decision points, signature contacts, proposed pilot start date.

Renewal/upsell tracker snippet (to paste into spreadsheet)
- Account name | ACV today | Renewal date | Proposed ARR uplift | Recommended path | Decision maker | Next meeting date | Status | Risk score
- Example row: AcmeApps | $180k | 2026-08-15 | +$60k | Private (VPC) | Kathleen Ross (CISO) | 2026-03-22 | negotiating | 3

Technical validation checklist (SE-driven)
- Network: VPC peering tested? (Y/N) — firewall rules required? — outbound egress cost estimate done?
- Auth: KMS integration proven? HSM required?
- Data: PII classification completed? Redaction/retention requirements noted?
- Performance: baseline p50/p95 latency, KV cache hit rate, batch size distribution collected.
- Ops: Log ingestion path, tracing hooks, backup policy.
- Pilot run: sample workload submitted (tokens, concurrent streams), success criteria defined.

Commercial guidance (CS + Sales collaboration)
- Pricing levers: reserved GPU capacity (committed monthly), concurrency slots, dedicated instance types, SLA premium (15–30%).
- Migration incentives: 10–20% one-time migration credit for multi-year commits.
- Contract language redlines to watch: data residency clause, termination for convenience, liability caps.

Outreach cadence (example sequence)
- Day 0: Internal intake + AE handoff (CSM)
- Day 3: Send technical pre-read + invite for 2-hour workshop (SE + CSM)
- Day 10: Workshop follow-up with architecture options and next-steps doc
- Day 14: Commercial sketch and optional ROI spreadsheet
- Day 21: Executive summary + request for decision (present at QBR)

Sample email snippets (short)
- Intro to tech workshop (from CSM):
  "Hi <Name>, thanks for agreeing to a short workshop. We're planning a focused 90m session to review architecture options for a Private deployment and confirm network/KMS constraints. Agenda attached. Can you confirm availability next week? — Ava"
- Post-QBR follow-up (proposal):
  "Appreciate the time today. Attached is the proposal sketch and migration plan. If this aligns, we'd like to start a 2-week pilot on <date> to prove performance. Next steps: internal approval -> pilot scoping -> contract. — Ava"

Risk signals and escalation matrix
- High risk (action now): repeated SLA misses, public incident, legal asks for on-prem or strict data residency within 90 days of renewal. Escalate to VP CS and Solutions Eng.
- Medium risk: steady spend growth but open security questions. Trigger SE deep-dive and legal pre-review.
- Low risk: healthy usage with no compliance asks — document opportunity and plan for next renewal.

Play tactics by buyer persona
- Platform/Infra (SRE): emphasize predictable latency, control plane isolation, observability integrations. Provide perf benchmarks and tracing examples.
- Security/CISO: provide KMS/HSM architecture, SOC2/ISO attachments, data flow maps. Offer pilot in redacted mode.
- Finance/Procurement: show cost-per-token economics, ROI model, and committed discount schedule.
- Product/ML lead: highlight model variants, latency benefits, and rollback/fallback policies.

Open questions / TODOs (placeholders)
- Confirm whether AcmeApps requires FIPS-certified HSM (ticket: CS-4123).
- Need updated latency benchmarks for dedicated G5-type instances (eng ticket PR-234).
- Pricing approval threshold for >$100k uplift — who signs for >$250k? (ask sales ops).

Owners & next steps (immediately actionable)
- Ava Martinez (CSM): schedule customer workshop, prep QBR slide deck (due 2026-03-15).
- Samir Patel (SE): run pilot workload and complete tech checklist (due 2026-03-29).
- Leah O'Connor (AE): draft commercial term sheet & commit levels (due 2026-03-22).

Notes to self (working/doc style)
- Keep the proposal modular: customers often pick hybrid — e.g., Dedicated + VPC + SLA.
- Watch for procurement timelines (large enterprises need 60–90 days for SOW/legal).
- Record every architecture variant in Confluence to speed future conversions.

Appendix: short scripts and negotiation prompts
- If asked to match price of competitor X: "We can discuss a committed capacity discount and migration credits; to do so we need a 12–24 month commit and a short pilot to validate performance guarantees."
- If asked about rollback: "We maintain the same API surface and fallback to hosted model variants during cutover; rollback runbook included in the migration plan."

Last saved notes:
- Drafted commercial uplift buckets: +10% (SLA only), +25% (Dedicated capacity tier up), +35–50% (Private + managed onboarding). Need legal to confirm SLA wording.
- Add a short appendix with a sample SOW checklist for Private deployments (network, storage, ops-runbook, support windows).

End of doc.

(Informal — intended as a working template; will refine after first real conversion sprint.)
